subject: english
question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

My years in my father’s house

A. would have been unbearable had

B. the feel of his hand clutching mine, his

C. I not had my brother. I never forgot

D. refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct sequence** of these sentences is **ACBD**. Here's why:
 
• "My years in my father’s house" is the main clause, which can stand by itself as a complete sentence.
 
• **"A. **would have been unbearable had" is the start of the next part of the sentence.
 
 
• **It provides a continuation** to the main clause, implying that something made the years bearable.
 
 
 
• **"C. **I not had my brother." This sentence fits well with the previous part (A) as it provides the answer to what made the years bearable - having a brother.
 
 
• **It forms a complete and meaningful sentence** when put after A, "My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother."
 
• "I never forgot" is the continuation of the first part of the sentence, focusing on the protagonist's memories related to his brother.
 
 
 
• **"B. **the feel of his hand clutching mine, his" This sentence logically follows the previous part (C) as it provides more specific memories of his brother.
 
• **"D. **refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise."
 
 
• This **sentence fits well **at the end as it rounds off the sentiment of the previous parts and completes the overall thought.
 
 

Therefore, the** complete sentence** is: *"My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother. I never forgot the feel of his hand clutching mine, his refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise." Hence, the correct sequence is ACBD.*
